claim_judgments.rationale: The claim asserts unconditionally that an employer must have an emergency action plan, completely omitting the governing condition 'whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one'. Consequently, the scope is overbroad, admitting cases where no OSHA standard in Part 1910 requires such a plan, and the summary fails to capture this core qualification and application rule.

The claim states that an emergency action plan must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available for review, but omits the explicit exception from the subsequent sentence permitting employers with 10 or fewer employees to communicate the plan orally. Because it fails to incorporate this exception, the scope is overbroad and the summary is incomplete.
The claim faithfully conveys the permissive exception allowing employers with 10 or fewer employees to communicate the plan orally to employees when required by an OSHA standard under this part.
The claim accurately reflects the requirement that an employer designate and train employees to assist in a safe and orderly evacuation of other employees under the governing scope of Part 1910.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 captures the general obligation to have an emergency action plan but omits the governing prerequisite that an OSHA standard in Part 1910 must require one, as well as the rule that Section 1910.38 applies to each such plan.

Claim C0001 captures the requirement for the plan to be written, kept in the workplace, and accessible, but omits the qualification regarding the oral communication exception for employers with 10 or fewer employees.
Claim C0002 fully and faithfully represents the permission for employers with 10 or fewer employees to communicate the plan orally.
No draft claim addresses the minimum plan requirement regarding procedures for reporting a fire or other emergency.
No draft claim addresses the minimum plan requirement regarding emergency evacuation procedures, types of evacuation, or exit route assignments.
No draft claim covers the requirement for procedures for employees who remain to operate critical plant operations before evacuating.
No draft claim addresses the requirement for procedures to account for all employees after evacuation.
No draft claim covers the requirement for procedures to be followed by employees performing rescue or medical duties.
No draft claim covers the requirement to include the name or job title of contact employees for plan information and duties.
No draft claim covers the employer duty to have and maintain an employee alarm system.
No draft claim addresses the alarm system requirements regarding distinctive signals and compliance with § 1910.165.
Claim C0003 fully covers the employer's duty to designate and train employees to assist in safe and orderly evacuations.
No draft claim covers the requirement to review the plan with covered employees upon development or initial job assignment.
No draft claim covers the requirement to review the plan when an employee's responsibilities under the plan change.
No draft claim covers the requirement to review the plan with covered employees when the plan is changed.
